scope: Forty benchmark candidates assessed in three rounds. The five remaining untranslated candidates reference continuations and were excluded at the user's request.
validation: Completed ports passed reduced-input correctness checks on Chez and the existing C build, upstream Guile checks with identical inputs, and targeted lint. No runtime changes. Canonical benchmark coverage is partial; see additional_validation.

maze.reason: The measured algorithm uses call-with-current-continuation, which is absent from the shared Otium API. No replacement algorithm or Chez escape hatch was used.

ctak.reason: The measured algorithm uses call-with-current-continuation, which is absent from the shared Otium API. No replacement algorithm or Chez escape hatch was used.

fibc.reason: The measured algorithm uses call-with-current-continuation, which is absent from the shared Otium API. No replacement algorithm or Chez escape hatch was used.

pi.reason: Requires exact-integer-sqrt inside the timed algorithm. The shared Otium API only exposes floating-point sqrt; both runtimes report E0201 for exact-integer-sqrt. Replacing it with floating-point arithmetic would lose integer precision, and implementing a new integer-root algorithm or using a Chez escape hatch was outside this translation pass.

chudnovsky.reason: Requires exact-integer-sqrt inside the timed algorithm. The shared Otium API only exposes floating-point sqrt; both runtimes report E0201 for exact-integer-sqrt. Replacing it with floating-point arithmetic would lose integer precision, and implementing a new integer-root algorithm or using a Chez escape hatch was outside this translation pass.

mbrotZ.reason: Requires native complex-number arithmetic, make-rectangular, real-part, and imag-part inside the timed algorithm. Both runtimes report E0201 for these complex-number procedures. Rewriting complex arithmetic as pairs of real values would change what mbrotZ measures, so no replacement was made.

browse.reason: Untimed database initialization wraps the pattern cursor explicitly instead of creating a cyclic pair list; the timed matching algorithm is retained.

checks.upstream_guile: 1200 pattern-match truth values agree with both runtimes

parsing.reason: The lexer uses a fixed-size mutable string token accumulator inside the measured parser. Shared make-string and string-set! are absent; both names report E0201 on Chez and C. Replacing the buffer with arrays or string concatenation would change measured allocation and mutation, so no substitute implementation was added.

slatex.reason: The formatter uses mutable string buffers throughout its timed line processing (slatex.make-line and slatex.get-line). Shared make-string and string-set! are unavailable. Replacing its string buffers and operations with a new representation would require a substantial port; no runtime changes or host escape hatches were made.
